line.gate_start: Chained. Dad never chained the gate. There's a gap in the fence further along.
line.fence: The gate's chained. The fence is broken to the right of it.
line.porch: Locked. Dad always kept a spare in the old bird box by the steps.
line.locked_front: Locked. The spare key... the bird box by the steps.
line.key: Still here. Some things don't change.
line.inside: It smells like meat left out in the sun. Lily? ...Lily?
line.phone_ans: That was Dad's voice. Dad's been dead for three weeks. Lily said so.
line.phone_ring: Dad's voice. On the machine. Recorded tonight.
line.phone_dead: The line is dead. It's been dead all night.
line.radio_done: The silo. Bolt cutters, barn workshop. And... don't go upstairs.
line.not_her: That's not her. That is not her voice. It's coming down.
line.escaped: It stopped at the door. It's letting me go. Why is it letting me go?
line.hide_ok: It went outside. Toward the barn.
line.sneaked: It didn't hear me. Barn. Now.
line.still_ok: It smelled me. It was right there, and it smelled me. And it left.
line.jumped: Get up. Keep moving. The shed is behind the barn.
line.shed: Oh god. Oh god, the smell. Don't look. Find the coat.
line.coat: Dad. I'm so sorry, Dad. ...The keys are in his pocket.
line.coat2: I can't look at him again.
line.crowbar: That'll open the tool cabinet in the workshop.
line.pitchfork: If it grabs me... at least I can make it let go.
line.gas_can: Gas. The truck will need it.
line.meat: It's hungry all the time. Lily said so.
line.toolcab_locked: Padlocked. I need something to pry it.
line.storage: Nailed shut from the inside. Someone wrote 'DON'T' on the boards.
line.silo_locked: Padlocked. I need the bolt cutters from the barn.
line.silo_later: Not yet. She said keys first, then come for her.
line.shed_locked: Dad's shed. Something is buzzing in there. Flies. Thousands of them.
line.clock: It stopped at 3:12. Every clock in the house stopped at 3:12.
line.stove: Still warm. Someone has been burning paper in here. Photographs.
line.stove2: Ash, and a melted wedding ring.
line.sink: The water runs red, then brown, then clear.
line.hamradio: Static. Under the static, someone is repeating my name.
line.hamradio2: A weather report from the county. 'Clear skies by morning.'
line.mirror: For a second, there were two of me in the mirror.
line.mirror2: Just me. I look like Dad.
line.bell: Stupid. Stupid! Everything for a mile heard that.
line.well: A long, long time before the splash.
line.generator_save: I need that gas for the truck.
line.tape_again: I can't listen to it again.
line.gate: Chained shut. The truck will go through it, or I'll cut it.
line.gate_truck: The truck can go through the gate.
line.truck_early: Dad's truck. No keys, no gas. Not yet.
line.truck_nokeys: The keys. Dad had the keys.
line.caught2: Keep the light off it. Keep low.
line.look_portrait: Grandpa Harrow. Somebody scratched his eyes out.
line.look_family: Our family. Mom's face has been burned off the photograph.
line.look_books: Almanacs. A Bible with half the pages torn out.
line.look_stove: Pots of something that boiled dry a long time ago.
line.look_antlers: Dad's first buck. The antlers are missing a tine. I know where it went.
line.look_tub: Don't look in the tub. Don't.
line.look_saddle: Mom's saddle. Nobody's ridden since she died.
line.look_drifter: He's been here a long time. He has no hands.
line.look_scarecrow: Bones, antlers and a feed sack. It made these. It's making a herd.
line.look_mailbox: HARROW. The flag is up. Nobody has collected the mail since August.

dlg.phone: The phone is ringing. Nobody has paid that bill since August.

sub.v.lily.vm1: Sam? It's Lily. I know it's late. I know you said never to call. Please... please just come home.
sub.v.lily.vm2: Something's wrong with Dad. He's not... it's not Dad anymore. It talks like him. It laughs like him.
sub.v.lily.vm3: It came out of the old cellar in the summer. It's been learning. It listens to everything we say.
sub.v.lily.vm4: Don't call the house. If it answers in my voice... hang up. I'm so sorry, Sam.
sub.v.lily.r1: Sam? Sam... is that you? Oh my god. You came.
sub.v.lily.r2: Shh, not so loud! I'm in the silo. Dad locked me in before... before it got him. It can't get in here.
sub.v.lily.r3: There's a padlock on the door. Dad's bolt cutters are in the barn workshop.
sub.v.lily.r4: Sam, listen to me. It copies voices. It's been using Dad's for weeks. If anyone says they're me, ask for the word.
sub.v.lily.r5: The word is butterscotch. Like Mom's candy.
sub.v.lily.r6: And Sam... whatever you hear in the house tonight... don't go upstairs.
sub.v.lily.r7: Sam? Did you get out of the house? Go to the barn. And be quiet in there. That's where it sleeps.
sub.v.lily.r8: Sam? Sam, are you there? Did you find them?
sub.v.lily.r9: Sam... the truck keys. Dad had them in his coat. He went to the shed that night... he never came back.
sub.v.lily.silo1: Sam? Is that... is that you?
sub.v.lily.silo3: I thought it was going to be you. Wearing your voice. I thought I'd never know.
sub.v.lily.end2: Don't let go of my hand. Not once.
sub.v.lily.field2: Sam! SAM! It's got me! Please!
sub.v.lily.corn: Sam! I'm in the corn! Get the truck started, I'll find you!
sub.v.lily.corn2: Sam, I'm okay! I'm hiding in the corn. Start the truck. I'll come to you. Don't come looking for me.
sub.v.mlily.up1: Sam? Sam, I'm up here! I got out! Come up, quick!
sub.v.mlily.word_bad: W-word? What word, Sam? Come up.
sub.v.mlily.truck1: Sam! Get in! Drive, it's right behind you!
sub.v.mlily.truck_bad: There's no time for this! Just drive!
sub.v.mlily.radio_end: Sam? Sam, come back. It's me. It's really me.

note.mimic.kitchen.title: A note in Lily's handwriting
note.mimic.kitchen.body:
Sam -

If you're reading this you came. I'm in the silo. Dad locked me in there before it got him, it's the only place with a steel door.

The walkie is on channel 3. TALK QUIET. It listens. It always listens.

If you hear me anywhere else, it is NOT me.

- L
note.mimic.clipping.title: Clipping, Cass County Ledger
note.mimic.clipping.body:
THIRD FARMHAND MISSING THIS SUMMER

Sheriff's deputies are asking for information about Dale Pruitt, 34, last seen hitchhiking toward the Harrow place on Route 9, where he had been promised a week's work.

Pruitt is the third transient laborer reported missing in the county since July. Walter Harrow told deputies that no one by that name had ever arrived.
note.mimic.journal1.title: Dad's journal - July
note.mimic.journal1.body:
July 9. Found the root cellar wall pushed in from the other side. Something has been living in the dirt under the house. Lost two calves this week.

July 14. I saw it. God help me, I saw it. Arms. Too many arms.

July 15. It spoke to me tonight in Martha's voice. Martha has been dead six years. It said my name the way she used to.
note.mimic.journal2.title: Dad's journal - August
note.mimic.journal2.body:
Aug 2. It only stays away when it's fed. The cattle are gone. I have done something I can never take back.

Aug 20. Lily asked who the man in the barn was. I told her a hired hand. She is not stupid.

Aug 30. It sits in the rafters and repeats things. Things I said in this barn twenty years ago. It has been listening to this family a long time.
note.mimic.sheriff.title: Letter from the Sheriff's Office
note.mimic.sheriff.body:
Mr. Harrow,

This office has received a third complaint regarding the smell from your property and the condition of your livestock fences.

A deputy will visit on the 4th. Please ensure the gate is open.

Sheriff R. Doyle

(Across the bottom, in Dad's hand: 'Doyle came. Doyle didn't leave.')

note.mimic.ledger.body:
AUG
 3 - 2 calves
 6 - heifer
 9 - heifer
12 - Pruitt
15 - the Mexican boy (didn't get his name)
18 - 3 hogs
21 - DOYLE
24 - nothing left in the pens
27 - it was in the house tonight

SEPT
 1 - it wants the girl
note.mimic.diary.title: Lily's diary
note.mimic.diary.body:
Dad stopped talking at dinner. He just listens. When I talk he moves his lips with me, like he's practicing.

I don't think that's Dad anymore. I think Dad has been gone for a while.

I called Sam today. I left a message. He won't come. Why would he come, after everything.

If he comes I need to tell him about the word.
note.mimic.drawing.title: A drawing, crayon on feed sack
note.mimic.drawing.body:
A tall black shape on the barn roof with six long arms.

Underneath, a child's handwriting, years old: 'THE MAN WHO LIVES UNDER THE HOUSE'.

And underneath that, newer, in Lily's grown-up hand: 'I drew this when I was six. Nobody believed me.'
note.mimic.funeral.title: Funeral card
note.mimic.funeral.body:
In loving memory of
MARTHA ANNE HARROW
1951 - 2018

'And the dead shall be raised incorruptible.'

On the back, in pencil: 'It wore her voice to the funeral. I heard it in the cornfield the whole service.'
note.mimic.mother.title: A letter from Mom, never sent
note.mimic.mother.body:
Walt,

I keep hearing the children calling me from the field at night. Both of them, together, in perfect unison.

The children are asleep in their beds when it happens. I have checked.

Please let's sell the farm. Please. Before it learns all of us.
note.mimic.cellar.title: Scrawled on the cellar wall
note.mimic.cellar.body:
IT CAME FROM HERE

The earth is pushed out of a hole in the wall, big enough for a man to crawl through. The edges are scored with long, parallel claw marks.

Someone has nailed a crucifix over the hole. Upside down. Or it fell.
note.mimic.silo.title: Lily's tally marks
note.mimic.silo.body:
Three rows of marks scratched into the steel. Days.

Under them: 'it walked around the silo all night saying my name in Sam's voice. sam has never been here. how does it know his voice.'

'oh god. the voicemail. it heard me record the voicemail.'
note.mimic.butcher.title: Dad's last list
note.mimic.butcher.body:
IF I DON'T COME BACK
- truck keys in my coat
- gas in the barn
- the zippo is in the dining room cabinet
- it hates fire. it hates fire more than anything
- don't open the silo for anyone who doesn't know the word
- I'm sorry, Lily.
- I'm sorry, Sam.
note.mimic.vet.title: Veterinary invoice
note.mimic.vet.body:
HARROW, W.
Call-out, after hours: 1 heifer, 'mauled'

Vet's note: 'Not a coyote. Not a bear. Bite radius I have no animal for. Recommend you contact Fish & Wildlife.'

(Unpaid.)
note.mimic.tape.title: Dad's tape (transcript)
note.mimic.tape.body:
"If you're hearing this, Sammy... then I'm dead, and you came home anyway. Stubborn. Like your mother.

It came up out of the root cellar in July. Hungry. I fed it the calves. Then the cows. Then the men who came asking for work.

It learns. Every word you say near it, it keeps. It talked to me in their voices. Now it talks in mine.

Don't trust anything that sounds like family tonight. Not even me. Get your sister and burn it. Burn it all."
